questions.q: Choose the correct verb: My grandmother ___ tea every morning.
questions.explanation: A habit with a singular subject takes the simple present with -s.

questions.q: Choose the correct verb: Listen! Someone ___ at the door.
questions.explanation: 'Listen!' points to an action happening now, so the present continuous is used.

questions.q: Choose the correct verb: I ___ him since childhood.
questions.explanation: 'Since childhood' with a state continuing to now needs the present perfect: have known.

questions.q: Choose the correct verb: The match ___ before we reached the ground.
questions.explanation: The match started before another past action, so the past perfect is used.

questions.q: Choose the correct verb: This time tomorrow, I ___ an exam.
questions.explanation: An action in progress at a particular future time takes the future continuous.

questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
options: When I will reach, I will call you.
If he will come, I will go.
When I reach home, I will call you.
I will call you when I will reach.
questions.explanation: After 'when' and 'if' referring to the future, the simple present is used, not 'will'.

questions.q: Change into the present perfect tense: 'They finished the project.'
questions.explanation: The present perfect uses have/has with the past participle.

questions.q: Correct the error: 'Since morning it is raining.'
questions.answer: It has been raining since morning.
keyPoints: present perfect continuous: has been raining
questions.explanation: An action that began in the past and still continues takes the present perfect continuous.

questions.q: Choose the correct verb: The flowers ___ beautiful.
questions.explanation: 'Flowers' is plural, so the verb is 'are'.

questions.q: Choose the correct verb: He ___ his homework daily.
questions.explanation: A singular subject takes 'does' in the simple present.

questions.q: Choose the correct verb: Everyone ___ invited to the party.
questions.explanation: 'Everyone' is singular, so it takes 'is'.

questions.q: Choose the correct verb: The principal and the teachers ___ present.
questions.explanation: Two subjects joined by 'and' are plural.

questions.q: Choose the correct verb: The quality of these mangoes ___ excellent.
questions.explanation: The subject is 'quality', which is singular.

questions.q: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
options: The cattle is grazing in the field.
The news were broadcast at nine.
Neither the boy nor the girl was absent.
questions.explanation: With 'neither ... nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject, 'girl', which is singular.

questions.q: Correct the error: 'The sceneries of Kashmir is charming.'
questions.answer: The scenery of Kashmir is charming.
keyPoints: scenery is uncountable and has no plural
questions.explanation: 'Scenery' is an uncountable noun.

questions.q: Complete and explain: 'The Arabian Nights ___ a collection of stories.'
questions.answer: is. The title names a single work, so it takes a singular verb even though it looks plural.
keyPoints: title of one book is singular
questions.explanation: The title of a single book or film takes a singular verb.

questions.q: Choose the correct article: I read ___ interesting article.
questions.explanation: 'Interesting' begins with a vowel sound, so 'an' is used.

questions.q: Choose the correct article: He bought ___ useful book.
questions.explanation: 'Useful' begins with a 'yoo' consonant sound, so 'a' is used.

questions.q: Choose the correct article: ___ Taj Mahal is in Agra.
questions.explanation: A well-known unique building takes the definite article.

questions.q: Choose the correct word: He has ___ interest in sports, so he rarely plays.
questions.explanation: 'Interest' is uncountable, and 'little' means hardly any.

questions.q: Choose the correct word: ___ student must carry an identity card.
questions.explanation: 'Every' is followed by a singular noun.

questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
options: The Mount Everest is the highest peak.
She is an one-rupee coin collector.
My brother wants to be an astronaut.
questions.explanation: 'Astronaut' begins with a vowel sound, so 'an' is correct.

questions.q: Fill in with 'some' or 'any': (a) I have ___ questions. (b) Do you have ___ questions?
questions.explanation: 'Some' is normally used in affirmative sentences and 'any' in questions and negatives.

questions.q: Explain the difference in meaning between 'a few' and 'few'.
questions.answer: 'A few' means some, a small number (a positive idea). 'Few' means hardly any (a negative idea).
questions.explanation: The article changes the meaning from positive to negative.

questions.q: Choose the correct word: The picture is hanging ___ the wall.
questions.explanation: 'On' is used for something attached to a surface.

questions.q: Choose the correct word: He jumped ___ the river.
questions.explanation: 'Into' shows movement to the inside of something.

questions.q: Choose the correct word: She is interested ___ painting.
questions.explanation: The adjective 'interested' is followed by 'in'.

questions.q: Choose the correct word: He has been absent ___ Monday.
questions.explanation: 'Since' is used with a point in time.

questions.q: Choose the correct word: She is poor, ___ she is happy.
questions.explanation: 'But' links two contrasting ideas.

questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
questions.explanation: Adjectives such as senior and junior are followed by 'to', not 'than'.

questions.q: Join using 'so that': 'She saved money. She could buy a bicycle.'
questions.answer: She saved money so that she could buy a bicycle.
questions.explanation: 'So that' joins a purpose clause to the main clause.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks with prepositions: 'The children were excited ___ the trip, and they thanked their teacher ___ organising it.'
questions.explanation: These words take fixed prepositions.

questions.q: Choose the correct word: Cats ___ see in dim light.
questions.explanation: 'Can' expresses ability.

questions.q: Choose the correct word: ___ I help you with your bag?
questions.explanation: 'Shall I...?' is used to offer help.

questions.q: Choose the correct word: She has worked for sixteen hours, so she ___ be very tired.
questions.explanation: 'Must' expresses a strong logical conclusion.

questions.q: Choose the correct word: You ___ better take a taxi; it is getting late.
questions.explanation: 'Had better' is a fixed expression for strong advice.

questions.q: Choose the correct word: I ___ rather walk than take a bus.
questions.explanation: 'Would rather' expresses preference.

questions.q: Which sentence expresses ability?
questions.explanation: 'Can speak' says that she is able to speak four languages.

questions.q: Rewrite using 'may': 'Perhaps it will rain tomorrow.'
questions.explanation: 'May' replaces 'perhaps ... will'.

questions.q: Explain the difference between 'He used to play cricket' and 'He is used to playing cricket'.
questions.answer: 'Used to play' describes a habit in the past that no longer exists. 'Is used to playing' means he is accustomed to playing now.
questions.explanation: The two structures look alike but have different meanings.

questions.q: Choose the correct verb: The thief ___ by the police.
questions.explanation: The thief receives the action, so the passive 'was caught' is used.

questions.q: Choose the correct verb: A new school ___ in our town.
questions.explanation: The school receives the action in progress: is being built.

questions.q: Choose the passive voice of: 'Mohan is writing a letter.'
options: A letter is written by Mohan.
A letter is being written by Mohan.
A letter was being written by Mohan.
A letter has been written by Mohan.
questions.explanation: Present continuous active becomes is/are being + past participle.

questions.q: Choose the passive voice of: 'They have sold the house.'
options: The house is sold by them.
The house was sold by them.
The house had been sold by them.
The house has been sold by them.
questions.explanation: Present perfect active becomes has/have been + past participle.

questions.q: Choose the passive voice of: 'Who broke the vase?'
options: By whom was the vase broken?
By whom the vase was broken?
Who is the vase broken by?
questions.explanation: 'Who' becomes 'By whom' and the verb moves to was + past participle.

questions.q: Which of these sentences cannot be changed into the passive voice?
questions.explanation: 'Shines' is intransitive, so there is no object to become the subject.

questions.q: Change into the passive voice: 'The principal gave the prizes.'
questions.answer: The prizes were given by the principal.
questions.explanation: Simple past passive: was/were + past participle.

questions.q: Change into the passive voice: 'Someone has stolen my bicycle.'
questions.explanation: The vague agent 'someone' is normally left out in the passive.

questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: Ravi said, 'We are late.'
options: Ravi said that they were late.
Ravi said that we were late.
Ravi said that they had been late.
Ravi said that he was late.
questions.explanation: 'We' becomes 'they' and 'are' becomes 'were'.

questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: She said, 'I have lost my pen.'
options: She said that she lost my pen.
She said that I had lost my pen.
She said that she had lost her pen.
She said that she would lose her pen.
questions.explanation: Present perfect becomes past perfect; 'I' and 'my' become 'she' and 'her'.

questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: He said, 'I will come tomorrow.'
options: He said that he will come the next day.
He said that I would come the next day.
He said that he came the next day.
He said that he would come the next day.
questions.explanation: 'Will' becomes 'would' and 'tomorrow' becomes 'the next day'.

questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: She asked me, 'Why are you crying?'
options: She asked me why was I crying.
She asked me why I was crying.
She asked me why you were crying.
She asked me that why I was crying.
questions.explanation: The wh-question keeps its question word but takes statement order.

questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: The officer said to the driver, 'Do not park here.'
options: The officer told the driver do not park here.
The officer said to the driver not park there.
The officer told the driver not to park there.
The officer told the driver that do not park there.
questions.explanation: A negative command is reported with 'told ... not to + verb', and 'here' becomes 'there'.

questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: Anu said, 'What a lovely garden!'
options: Anu exclaimed with delight that it was a lovely garden.
Anu said what a lovely garden!
Anu asked what a lovely garden it was.
Anu exclaimed that she had a lovely garden.
questions.explanation: An exclamation is reported as a statement with 'exclaimed with delight that'.

questions.q: Change into indirect speech: The boy said to his father, 'I need a new bag.'
questions.answer: The boy told his father that he needed a new bag.
questions.explanation: The present tense moves back to the past tense.

questions.q: Change into direct speech: The teacher asked Mohan why he had not done his homework.
questions.answer: The teacher said to Mohan, 'Why have you not done your homework?'
keyPoints: he becomes you, his becomes your, had not done becomes have not done
questions.explanation: A reported wh-question becomes a direct question again.

questions.q: A sentence that gives an order or a request is called
questions.explanation: An imperative sentence gives a command or request.

questions.q: What kind of sentence is this? 'He is rich, yet he is unhappy.'
questions.explanation: Two independent clauses are joined by 'yet', a coordinating conjunction.

questions.q: Combine using 'although': 'She is old. She works hard.'
options: Although she is old and works hard.
She works hard although old she is.
She is old although she works hard.
Although she is old, she works hard.
questions.explanation: 'Although' introduces the concession, followed by the main clause.

questions.q: Change into an interrogative sentence: 'He is a doctor.'
questions.explanation: The verb 'is' is moved before the subject to form a question.

questions.q: Which sentence means the same as 'Sita is wiser than Gita'?
options: Gita is as wise as Sita.
Sita is not as wise as Gita.
Gita is not so wise as Sita.
questions.explanation: If Sita is wiser, then Gita is not so wise as Sita.

questions.q: Which sentence contains an adverb clause of reason?
options: She was happy because she had passed.
She said that she had passed.
The girl who passed is happy.
questions.explanation: 'Because she had passed' gives the reason for her happiness.

questions.q: Change into a complex sentence: 'Hearing the news, she wept.'
questions.answer: When she heard the news, she wept.
keyPoints: participle phrase becomes a subordinate clause
questions.explanation: A participle phrase can be expanded into an adverb clause of time.

questions.q: Combine using 'neither ... nor': 'He did not call. He did not write.'
keyPoints: neither ... nor joins the two verbs
questions.explanation: 'Neither ... nor' already contains the negation.

questions.q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
questions.explanation: 'It's' is the contraction of 'it is' and needs an apostrophe.

questions.q: Which sentence uses capital letters correctly?
options: Diwali is a festival of lights.
questions.explanation: The first word of a sentence and the name of a festival begin with capitals.

questions.q: Which sentence uses the comma correctly?
options: After the match, the players went home.
After the match the players, went home.
After, the match the players went home.
After the match the players went, home.
questions.explanation: A comma follows an introductory phrase.

questions.q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
questions.explanation: A comma introduces the quotation, and the full stop goes inside the closing quotation mark.

questions.q: Which sentence has the apostrophe in the correct place?
questions.explanation: The apostrophe takes the place of the missing letter o in 'do not'.

questions.q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
options: My favourite fruits are: mangoes, grapes and apples.
I bought a bag; a pen; and a book.
He was late; therefore, he missed the bus.
He was late, therefore he missed the bus.
questions.explanation: A semicolon joins two independent clauses, with a comma after 'therefore'.

questions.q: Punctuate correctly: what a beautiful sunset exclaimed the tourist
questions.answer: 'What a beautiful sunset!' exclaimed the tourist.
keyPoints: exclamation mark inside the inverted commas
questions.explanation: The exclamation stays inside the quotation marks.

questions.q: Give one use of the semicolon, with an example.
questions.answer: A semicolon joins two closely related independent clauses: She was tired; she went to bed early.
questions.explanation: A semicolon is stronger than a comma but weaker than a full stop.

questions.q: Choose the synonym of 'assist'.
questions.explanation: 'Assist' means to help.

questions.q: Choose the antonym of 'expand'.
questions.explanation: To expand is to become larger; to shrink is to become smaller.

questions.q: A collection of poems or other literary pieces is called a(n)
questions.explanation: An anthology is a collection of selected writings.

questions.q: Choose the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Accommodation' has double c and double m.

questions.q: The suffix -able in 'readable' means
questions.explanation: Readable means capable of being read.

questions.q: If an argument is 'cogent', it is
questions.explanation: A cogent argument is clear, logical and convincing.

questions.q: Write the opposites of 'increase', 'accept' and 'polite'.
questions.explanation: Antonyms have opposite meanings.

questions.q: Explain the difference between 'stationary' and 'stationery'.
questions.answer: 'Stationary' means not moving. 'Stationery' means writing materials such as pens and paper.
questions.explanation: The words sound alike but are spelt and used differently.

questions.q: What does the idiom 'to pull someone's leg' mean?
questions.explanation: It means to joke with or tease someone.

questions.q: What does the idiom 'at the eleventh hour' mean?
questions.explanation: It means at the last possible moment.

questions.q: What does the idiom 'to keep an eye on' mean?
questions.explanation: It means to watch something or someone carefully.

questions.q: What does the idiom 'to beat around the bush' mean?
options: to avoid coming to the point
questions.explanation: It means to talk about unimportant matters instead of the main point.

questions.q: What does the phrasal verb 'turn down' mean in 'She turned down the offer'?
questions.explanation: 'Turn down' means to refuse.

questions.q: Choose the correct phrasal verb: The company decided to ___ a new branch in Surat.
questions.explanation: 'Set up' means to establish something.

questions.q: Explain the idiom 'a storm in a teacup' and use it in a sentence.
questions.answer: It means a lot of fuss about something unimportant: The argument over the seat was a storm in a teacup.
keyPoints: means excitement over a trivial matter
questions.explanation: The idiom describes a small problem treated as a big one.

questions.q: Explain the phrasal verb 'break down' and use it in a sentence.
questions.answer: 'Break down' means to stop working (of a machine): Our car broke down on the highway.
keyPoints: means to stop working or fail
questions.explanation: It is commonly used for vehicles and machines.

questions.q: Read the passage. 'Kabir's father repairs bicycles in a tiny shop near the bus stand. Kabir often helps him after school by pumping air into tyres. Though the shop earns little, his father says that honest work is its own reward. Kabir has decided that when he grows up, he will open a bigger workshop and teach other young people the trade.' What does Kabir's father do?
questions.explanation: He repairs bicycles in a tiny shop.

questions.q: Read the passage. 'Kabir's father repairs bicycles in a tiny shop near the bus stand. Kabir often helps him after school by pumping air into tyres. Though the shop earns little, his father says that honest work is its own reward. Kabir has decided that when he grows up, he will open a bigger workshop and teach other young people the trade.' How does Kabir help his father?
questions.explanation: The passage says he pumps air into tyres after school.

questions.q: Read the passage. 'Kabir's father repairs bicycles in a tiny shop near the bus stand. Kabir often helps him after school by pumping air into tyres. Though the shop earns little, his father says that honest work is its own reward. Kabir has decided that when he grows up, he will open a bigger workshop and teach other young people the trade.' What does Kabir's plan show?
options: He respects his father's work and wants to carry it forward
He wants to leave the town
He thinks the shop earns too much
questions.explanation: He wants to grow the same trade and teach others.

questions.q: Read the passage. 'Kabir's father repairs bicycles in a tiny shop near the bus stand. Kabir often helps him after school by pumping air into tyres. Though the shop earns little, his father says that honest work is its own reward. Kabir has decided that when he grows up, he will open a bigger workshop and teach other young people the trade.' What does Kabir's father believe about honest work?
questions.answer: He believes that honest work is its own reward, even if it earns little money.
keyPoints: honest work is its own reward
money earned is not the only measure
questions.explanation: The passage quotes this belief.

questions.q: Read the passage. 'Sound travels in waves. These waves move through air, water and solids, but they cannot travel through empty space because there is nothing to carry them. This is why astronauts working outside a spacecraft cannot hear each other without radios.' Through which of these can sound travel?
questions.explanation: The passage lists air, water and solids.

questions.q: Read the passage. 'Sound travels in waves. These waves move through air, water and solids, but they cannot travel through empty space because there is nothing to carry them. This is why astronauts working outside a spacecraft cannot hear each other without radios.' Why can sound not travel through empty space?
options: There is nothing to carry the waves
questions.explanation: The passage says there is nothing to carry the waves.

questions.q: Read the passage. 'Sound travels in waves. These waves move through air, water and solids, but they cannot travel through empty space because there is nothing to carry them. This is why astronauts working outside a spacecraft cannot hear each other without radios.' What does the example of the astronauts show?
options: Sound needs a material to travel through, which space lacks
questions.explanation: It illustrates that sound cannot cross empty space.

questions.q: Read the passage. 'Sound travels in waves. These waves move through air, water and solids, but they cannot travel through empty space because there is nothing to carry them. This is why astronauts working outside a spacecraft cannot hear each other without radios.' Why do astronauts need radios to talk outside their spacecraft?
questions.answer: Outside the spacecraft there is empty space with nothing to carry sound waves, so they cannot hear each other without radios.
keyPoints: sound waves need something to travel through
questions.explanation: The passage gives this cause directly.

questions.q: Read the passage. 'Neha found a wallet on the pavement outside the market. Inside were some money and a card with an address. Though she was tempted to keep the money for a new book, she remembered how worried her mother had been when she once lost her purse. She walked three streets to the address and returned the wallet to its grateful owner.' Where did Neha find the wallet?
options: On the pavement outside the market
questions.explanation: She found it on the pavement outside the market.

questions.q: Read the passage. 'Neha found a wallet on the pavement outside the market. Inside were some money and a card with an address. Though she was tempted to keep the money for a new book, she remembered how worried her mother had been when she once lost her purse. She walked three streets to the address and returned the wallet to its grateful owner.' What helped Neha decide to return the wallet?
options: She remembered her mother's worry when she lost a purse
She did not need a book
questions.explanation: The memory of her mother's worry changed her mind.

questions.q: Read the passage. 'Neha found a wallet on the pavement outside the market. Inside were some money and a card with an address. Though she was tempted to keep the money for a new book, she remembered how worried her mother had been when she once lost her purse. She walked three streets to the address and returned the wallet to its grateful owner.' In the passage, 'tempted' means
questions.explanation: She was strongly drawn to keeping the money for a book.

questions.q: Read the passage. 'Neha found a wallet on the pavement outside the market. Inside were some money and a card with an address. Though she was tempted to keep the money for a new book, she remembered how worried her mother had been when she once lost her purse. She walked three streets to the address and returned the wallet to its grateful owner.' What does Neha's action show about her character? Support your answer from the passage.
questions.answer: She is honest and thoughtful. She resisted the temptation to keep the money, thought of how the owner would feel, and walked three streets to return the wallet.
keyPoints: took trouble to return the wallet
questions.explanation: Her choices show honesty and empathy.

questions.q: Read the passage. 'A rainbow appears when sunlight passes through raindrops. The drops bend and split the light into its colours, which spread out in a curved band. To see a rainbow, you must stand with the sun behind you and the raindrops in front of you.' When does a rainbow appear?
questions.explanation: The first sentence states this.

questions.q: Read the passage. 'A rainbow appears when sunlight passes through raindrops. The drops bend and split the light into its colours, which spread out in a curved band. To see a rainbow, you must stand with the sun behind you and the raindrops in front of you.' Where must you stand to see a rainbow?
options: With the sun behind you and the rain in front
questions.explanation: The last sentence gives this position.

questions.q: Read the passage. 'A rainbow appears when sunlight passes through raindrops. The drops bend and split the light into its colours, which spread out in a curved band. To see a rainbow, you must stand with the sun behind you and the raindrops in front of you.' What do raindrops do to sunlight?
options: Bend and split it into colours
questions.explanation: The drops bend and split the light into its colours.

questions.q: Read the passage. 'A rainbow appears when sunlight passes through raindrops. The drops bend and split the light into its colours, which spread out in a curved band. To see a rainbow, you must stand with the sun behind you and the raindrops in front of you.' Explain how a rainbow is formed.
questions.answer: Sunlight passes through raindrops, which bend and split it into its colours; the colours spread out as a curved band.
keyPoints: drops bend and split the light into colours
questions.explanation: The passage describes the steps.
